root_cause.text: In `kernel/bpf/verifier.c`’s `adjust_reg_min_max_vals()`, the linked-register delta tracking for ALU add/sub operations reads `src_reg` after `dst_reg` has already been modified in-place, so when `src_reg == dst_reg` (e.g. `rX += rX`) it computes the delta from the updated value instead of the original source and propagates a wrong offset via `sync_linked_regs()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a guard to skip `BPF_SRC(insn->code) == BPF_X && insn->src_reg == insn->dst_reg` in the `is_reg_const(src_reg, alu32)` delta-tracking block, and the commit message explicitly says `dst_reg` is modified first and then `reg_const_value(src_reg)` reads the post-{add,sub} value, causing an incorrect delta and verifier-vs-runtime mismatch.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip constant min/max adjustment for self-referential register add/sub instructions to avoid incorrect verifier range tracking.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the constant-add/subtract range adjustment in `adjust_reg_min_max_vals()` was extended with an extra check that rejects cases where the instruction is register-sourced (`BPF_SRC(insn->code) == BPF_X`) and the source and destination registers are the same (`insn->src_reg == insn->dst_reg`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the verifier will no longer apply this constant-folding min/max adjustment when an ALU add/sub instruction reads and writes the same register. This prevents the constant-based range update from being incorrectly applied in self-referential register operations, preserving verifier state accuracy.
